rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperfect verb presents the proof as renewed continually through recurring messengers and recitation.
rows.anchor: عبر بالمضارع لتجدد البيان في كل وقت بتجدد الرسال والتلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bayyina is the Messenger together with his signs, above all the revealed Book, whether Torah, Gospel, Psalms, or Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو الرسول وما معه من الآيات التي أعظمها الكتاب سواء كان التوراة أو الإنجيل أو الزبور أو الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣuḥuf literally means sheets or paper, but here denotes their contents because of their close association.
rows.anchor: جمع صحيفة وهي القرطاس والمراد ما فيها , عبر بها عنه لشدة المواصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pages are purified from idolatry and every deviation; falsehood cannot approach them, and only the purified touch them.
rows.anchor: الباطل من الشرك بالأوثان وغيرها من كل زيغ لا يأتيها من بين يديها ولا من خلفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although unlettered, the Messenger's recitation counts as reading what is contained in the pages.
rows.anchor: وقراءته وإن كان أميا لمثل ما فيها قراءة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The writings contain precious knowledge and are wholly upright because they speak truth without shirk or any kind of crookedness.
rows.anchor: هي في غاية الاستقامة لنطقها بالحق الذي لا مرية فيه ليس فيها شرك ولا عوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Before the proof arrived, People of the Book believed in the Prophet because of explicit glad tidings, while polytheists claimed a warner would make them better guided; his arrival divided both groups into believers and rejecters.
rows.anchor: أهل الكتاب يؤمنون بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم لما عندهم من البشائر الصريحة به

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: The surah continues the prior account of reciting the Book and the night of its revelation, stressing that Jews had invoked and praised the promised Book and messenger but became its first rejecters when they appeared.
rows.anchor: هي من كمال ما تقدمها لأنه لما أمره عليه الصلاة والسلام بقراءة كتابه الذي به اتضحت سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book and its bearer had been foretold in Torah and Gospel, and People of the Book had hoped to gain victory over their enemies through him; those without prior knowledge, such as Abu Bakr and Umar, were blessed for accepting him, whereas informed rejecters became the worst creation.
rows.anchor: وقد كانوا يؤملون الانتصار به عليه الصلاة والسلام من أعدائهم ويستفتحون بكتابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the proof came, the Prophet divided the people into guided and astray, and Arabs only united upon guidance after it arrived.
rows.anchor: ثم ما اجتمع العرب على الهدى إلا من بعد ما جاءتهم البينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People given scripture dispersed from their adherence or promise to follow the expected truth in Muhammad; as with Jesus, some persisted in error and broke their covenant while others kept the promise and were guided.
rows.anchor: عما كانوا عليه من الإطباق على الضلال أو الوعد باتباع الحق المنتظر في محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their split lasted only briefly; the few who believed did not count as a lasting division among the many who remained astray.
rows.anchor: وكان تفرقهم لم يعد تفرقا إلا زمنا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among converts were formerly Christian Arab tribes including Tanukh, Ghassan, Amila, Bakr b. Wa'il, and Abd al-Qays, as well as Jews from Yemen.
rows.anchor: بإسلام من أسلم من قبائل العرب الذين كانوا قد أطبقوا على النصرانية من تنوخ وغسان وعاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their response matched 2:89: when the proof they recognized arrived, they disbelieved in it.
rows.anchor: فلما جاءهم ما عرفوا كفروا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Polytheists split only briefly at first and later united in guidance, which the author attributes to their sound natural disposition; this contrast reveals the greater crookedness and stubbornness of learned People of the Book.
rows.anchor: فكان الضال منهم أكثر , ثم أطبقوا على الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's explanation for learned rejecters' obduracy is accumulated moral corruption: illicit gain, major sins, and postponing repentance darken and rust the heart until it cannot respond to guidance.
rows.anchor: من قوة ما لطباعهم من كدر النقص بتربيته وتنميته بالمعاصي من أمل السحت من الربا وغيره من الكبائر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse emphasizes the manifest command to obey rather than identifying the commander, and the commands are contained in the books whose observance is binding.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المقصود بروز الأمر المطاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship is carrying out God's command in its prescribed form with utmost love, humility, and reverence, while keeping a moderate pace to avoid fatigue or self-admiration.
rows.anchor: مع المبادر بغاية الحب والخضوع والتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere religion excludes overt and hidden shirk: obedience is for God's pleasure because He commanded it, not to obtain benefit or avert harm.
rows.anchor: بأن يكون الامتثال لكونه أمر لرضاه لا لشي من نفع ولا دفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Correct foundations matter: pure activity built on a corrupt basis is fruitless or harmful, as with monks and people who follow someone they cannot distinguish from an enemy or one being deluded by apparent favor.
rows.anchor: ويكون بناؤه بغير أساس صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He defines sincerity as directing obedience solely to God, forgetting other people in one's acts and avoiding self-regard by seeing oneself only as a commanded servant.
rows.anchor: إفراد الحق في الطاعة بالقصد مع نسيان الخلق في الأعمال والتوصل إليه بالتوقي من ملاحظتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites 23:60 to connect sincere practice with hearts remaining apprehensive about returning to God.
rows.anchor: يؤتون ما آتوا وقلوبهم وجلة أنهم إلى ربهم راجعون

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri defines sincerity as purifying an act from defects.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري : ويقال : الإخلاص تصفية العمل من الخلل

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls sincerity a pure intention: intention persists while action stops, action needs intention, and intention does not need action.
rows.anchor: وقال الرازي : الإخلاص النية الصافية لأن النية دائمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥanīfs are deeply inclined toward evidence and abandon even slight deviation when it conflicts with proof, thereby attaining uprightness.
rows.anchor: في غاية الميل مع الدليل إلى القوم بحيث لا يكون عندهم اعوجاج أصلا

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malawi says the language's general sense of inclination was conventionally restricted to inclination toward good; the name al-Ahnaf reflects feet that turn inward.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي : وخصه العرف بالميل إلى الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Absolute ḥanīfiyya renounces the five false religious roots and their branches, moving from false belief to truth, sins to good works, disliked acts to recommended ones, excess to restraint, and its causes to asceticism.
rows.anchor: متبرئا عن أصول الملل الخمس : اليهود والنصارى والصابئين والمجوس والمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse combines sincerity toward God and renunciation of other creatures; the latter is expressed through fear, which redirects the worshipper to God and what pleases Him.
rows.anchor: فالآية جامعة لمقامي الإخلاص الناظر أحدهما إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Establishing prayer means making it upright with all its conditions, pillars, and limits; prayer is reverence for God's command.
rows.anchor: بجميع الشرائط والأركان والحدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakat completes the relation to creation by delivering it to its rightful recipients to support religion, and its broader spiritual sense includes every gift such as intellect, senses, limbs, and influence.
rows.anchor: وتدخل الزكاة عند أهل الله في كل ما رزق الله من عقل وسمع وبصر ولسان ويد ورجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean the religion of the upright community, souls, or books; on the first reading it is an annexation of a described noun to its quality.
rows.anchor: أي الملة أو النفوس أو الكتب التي لا عوج فيها

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil reads al-qayyima as the plural of qayyim, synonymous with qā'im, meaning the religion of those who stand before God in monotheism.
rows.anchor: وعن الخليل أنه قال : هو جمع قيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past-tense description of those who disbelieved denotes people who veiled reason's signs through defective reasoning and persisted in error; People of the Book means Jews and Christians, while the polytheists are deeply rooted in shirk.
rows.anchor: وقع منهم الستر لمرائي عقولهم بعد صرفها للنظر الصحيح فضلوا واستمروا على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift from a verb for the earlier polytheists to a descriptive noun here suggests that an unentrenched polytheist may leave shirk, whereas even slight attachment to disbelief makes a learned person less likely to return.
rows.anchor: ودل بالإتيان بالوصف هنا والفعل في أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two groups share the general kind of punishment, but the intensity and type differ according to the degree of their disbelief.
rows.anchor: واشتراك الفريقين في جنس العذاب لا يوجب التساوي في النوع بل يختلف بحسب اشتداد الكفر وخفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rejecters are the worst of creation: they neglected self-reform and their own needs, making that designation a fire for their souls.
rows.anchor: الذين أهملوا إصلاح أنفسهم , وفرطوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers include the whole created order, angels and others, and righteous deeds confirm their faith; the heart's reward is named before bodily reward because it is greater.
rows.anchor: أقروا بالإيمان من الخلق كلهم الملائكة وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful are the best of creation and are elevated in rank.
rows.anchor: العالو الدرجات { هم } أي خاصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reward is lasting Gardens of Eden, where rivers flow continuously beneath their land, rooms, and trees; permanence is emphasized to intensify the promise.
rows.anchor: أي إقامة لا تحول عنها { تجري } أي جريا دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's pleasure follows prior care and guidance; believers are pleased because every wish is granted, while recognizing that all is grace and God owes no creature anything.
rows.anchor: أي بما كان سبق لهم من العناية والتوفيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greatest divine favor is their following the Messenger, the cause of every good; the promise is generalized to anyone whose fitting fear of the Lord prevents procrastination and forbidden desire.
rows.anchor: وأعظم نعمه عليهم ما من عليهم به من متابعتهم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Continuous divine favor should increase fear and thus gratitude; fear is the source of every good and a defining quality of knowers.
rows.anchor: فإن الخشية ملاك الأمر , والباعث على كل خير

rows.speaker: الملوي
rows.claim: Al-Malawi distinguishes fear as anxious loss of security, intensified into wajal and then rahba that causes flight; love brings awe, while overwhelming awareness of majesty brings reverence.
rows.anchor: قال الملوي ما معناه : إن الإنسان إذا استشعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who fears God leaves whatever is unfitting for Him, does not doubt the proof, and keeps fear in the heart, which the surah links back to its opening division between those who escape desire and those ruined by it.
rows.anchor: فمن خاف ربه هذا الخوف انفك من جميع ما عنده مما لا يليق بجنابه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah divides people into one group freed from the soul's desire and saved, and another remaining its captive and destroyed.
rows.anchor: وبتصنيف الناس صنفي , ك صنف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's prior account says the Prophet specifically recited this surah to Ubayy after a reading dispute with two Companions; their readings were approved, and Ubayy then felt a doubt more severe than his pre-Islamic doubt.
rows.anchor: أنه وجد اثنين من الصحابة رضي الله عنهم قد خالفاه في القراءة فرفعهما إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ubayy says the Prophet struck his chest, he broke into a sweat, and the Prophet explained that the Qur'an was revealed in seven aḥruf.
rows.anchor: فضرب صلى الله عليه وسلم في صدري ففضت عرقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disputed reading occurred in al-Naḥl, whose themes this short surah condenses: prophetic witness, the Book's guidance and mercy, Gabriel strengthening believers, and the Jews' disagreement over Sabbath; Bayyina also warns against doubt after clear proof.
rows.anchor: على قصرها حاوية إجمالا لكل ما في النحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's concise reminder helped Ubayy grasp the warning quickly and retain it deeply, and God granted him steadfastness.
rows.anchor: ليكون أسرع له تصورا فيكون أرسخ في النفس وأثبت في القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet called Ubayy the most proficient reciter; Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah transmit it from Anas, the author grades it authentic, and some transmit it mursal.
rows.anchor: رواه أحمد والترمذي وابن ماجه عن أنس رضي الله تعالى عنه وهو صحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author warns that status should not prevent learning from someone of lower rank; many People of the Book rejected Islam because they compared their scriptural learning with the Arabs' ignorance rather than their present message.
rows.anchor: حتى لا يمنع أحدا ما يراه من علوه من القراءة على من هو دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's aim is to unveil realities and destiny fully, then divide people in the enduring abode into happiness and misery; its name points to this through the relation between the container and what it contains and the vicissitudes of divine decree.
rows.anchor: مقصودها انكشاف الأمور ، وظهور المقدور أتم ظهور ، وانقسام الناس في الجزاء في دار البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God's encompassing power and knowledge, mercy to all creation through outward blessings, and completion of blessing for His elect inwardly and outwardly.
rows.anchor: المحيط بكل شيء قدؤرة وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's aim is to unveil realities and destiny fully, then divide people in the enduring abode into happiness and misery; its name points to this through the relation between the container and what it contains and the vicissitudes of divine decree.
rows.anchor: مقصودها انكشاف الأمور ، وظهور المقدور أتم ظهور ، وانقسام الناس في الجزاء في دار البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God's encompassing power and knowledge, mercy to all creation through outward blessings, and completion of blessing for His elect inwardly and outwardly.
rows.anchor: المحيط بكل شيء قدؤرة وعلما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah follows al-Bayyina's account of recompense in the next life by describing that abode's initial events; al-Qāriʿa will describe later stages and final outcomes, sharpening warning by disclosing recompense.
rows.anchor: لما ختم تلك بجزاء الصالح والطالح في دار البقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle idhā signals a certain event, while the passive earthquake construction presents the action as extremely easy; it is the universal quake after the second blast, unlike earlier localized quakes.
rows.anchor: فقال معبرا بأداة التحقق لأن الأمر حتم لا بد من كونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quake is left undefined to let the mind imagine its magnitude; kasra makes zalzāl a verbal noun, whereas fatḥa would make it a name for movement, a distinction al-Bayḍāwī says occurs only in doubled forms.
rows.anchor: قال البيضاوي : وليس إلا في المضاعف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quake is proportionate to the immense earth and the greatness of that day, like giving a pious person honor suited to him.
rows.anchor: اضطرابها الذي يحق لها في مناسبته لعظمة جرم الأرض وعظمة ذلك اليوم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Al-Zubayr says the surah follows al-Bayyina to complete its brief account of the two groups by showing their fates and the recompense of each.
rows.anchor: وردت عقب سورة البرية ليبين بها حصول جزاء الفريقين ومآل الصنفين المذكورين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole earth brings out everything buried in it, including the dead and hidden treasures, after the quake of resurrection; what lies above ground is also a weight upon it.
rows.anchor: أي مما هو مدفون فيها كاأموات والكنوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As shaking a mat releases dirt from its folds, God's power to bring forth delicate plants through hard earth and break hard seeds demonstrates His power to recreate the dead; this is no harder than forming a fetus.
rows.anchor: فالذي قدر على ذلك هو سبحانه وتعالى قادر على تكوين الموتى في بطن الأرض وإعادتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans, forgetful and absorbed in themselves, ask in amazement or confusion what has happened to the earth; the speaker may be humanity generally or specifically a disbeliever.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التعجب والدهش أو الحيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbeliever's question resembles 36:52, to which the believer answers that this is what the Merciful promised and the messengers affirmed.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون القائل الكافر كما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth recounts the deeds for which it shook and brought forth its contents; everything done upon it becomes testimony against its actors.
rows.anchor: وكل شيء عمل عليها شهادة منها على العاملين

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud says the earth will tell its news in spoken words.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : تحدث بلسان المقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth's testimony enumerates each person's deeds: sinners will wish to be hurried to Hell to escape the shame, while believers rejoice at the testimony; even every moist and dry thing testifies for the caller to prayer as far as his voice reaches.
rows.anchor: تقول : عمل فلان كذا وكذا - تعدد حتى يود المجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because nothing occurs except by God's permission and passive constructions might hide the agent, the earth's report is caused by its Lord inspiring it; the lām signals swift enactment of that inspiration.
rows.anchor: ولما كان من المقرر أنه لا يكون شيء إلا بإذنه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After rising from the graves, people return swiftly and knowingly to the place where they are summoned before their Lord for judgment, separated by rank and condition as believers or disbelievers, safe or afraid, obedient or sinful.
rows.anchor: يرجع رجوعا هو في غاية السرعة والاهتداء إلى الموضع الذي ينادون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing their deeds may occur through whichever of God's hosts He chooses or directly, when God speaks to each person without interpreter or intermediary; alternatively, people depart the judgment place for their homes to see their recompense.
rows.anchor: حين يكلم سبحانه وتعالى كل أحد من غير ترجمان ولا واسطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every person, Muslim or disbeliever, sees even an atom's weight of good or evil because the Judge knows and can account for everything; a disbeliever's good was either rewarded in this life or nullified for lacking faith, while the believer rejoices in good and in evil that has been forgiven.
rows.anchor: فالكافر يوقف على أنه جوزي به في الدنيا أو أنه أحبط لبنائه على غير أساس الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dharra means either a tiny ant or a mote visible as it floats in a sunbeam through a window.
rows.anchor: والذرة النملة الصغيرة أو الهباءة التي ترى طائرة في الشعاع الداخل من الكوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's ending returns to its opening by telling news and exposing secrets; the author says a report of an unnamed Bedouin calls the final verse comprehensive, Ibn Masud calls it the Qur'an's most decisive verse, and the Prophet calls the surah al-fādhadha al-jāmiʿa.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : إنها أحكم آية في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet warned Aisha not to treat small sins lightly, since they accumulate and bring an account from God.
rows.anchor: إياك ومحقرات الذنوب , فإن لها من الله طالبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reports claims that the surah equals half the Qur'an and one quarter, and says they do not conflict: one measures its comprehensive afterlife rulings, the other its account of resurrection as one of four parts of complete faith.
rows.anchor: وروي كما ذكرته في كتابي ( مصاعد النظر في الإشراف على مقاصد السور )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tirmidhi transmits from Ali a Prophetic report that complete faith requires belief in God's oneness and Muhammad's mission, death, resurrection, and divine decree; the author uses it to count belief in resurrection as one quarter of faith.
rows.anchor: الحديث الذي رواه الترمذي عن علي رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( لا يؤمن عبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author further partitions religion into God's concern, the servants' concern, and worship in its hidden and public forms, associating Sūrat al-Naṣr with public worship.
rows.anchor: وأيضا فأمر الدين أربع أجزاء : أمر المعبود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿĀdiyāt warns that most people will perish on the earthquake day because they prefer transient status and wealth over what lasts with the Lord; its oath and subject signal this purpose.
rows.anchor: أكثر الخلق يوم الزلزلة هالك لإيثار الفاني من العز والمال على الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chapter's name most clearly points to its subject through reflection on the oath and what is sworn to.
rows.anchor: وقد علم أن اسمها أدل شيء على ذلك لما هدى إليه القسم والمقسم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God's complete command, universal gifts of creation and clarification, and special completion of blessing for His elect through guidance.
rows.anchor: الذي له الأمر كله فلا يسأل عما يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since wealth is transient, a sensible person should not attach hope to it in preference to what lasts; this question warns the forgetful person about the outcome of his affair.
rows.anchor: ولما كان المال فانيا لا ينبغي لعاقل أن يعلق أمله به فضلا عن أن يؤثرة الباقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive baʿthara stresses how easily the hidden is stirred up; it means to raise, bring out, scatter, inspect, and search with complete ease.
rows.anchor: أثير بغاية السهورة وأخرج وفرق ونظر وفتش بغاية السهولة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The graves contain dead people whom Arabs denied would be resurrected; their whole bodies are restored and their souls returned, so each person is raised as he died.
rows.anchor: فنشروا للحساب , أو من عظامهم ولحومهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning concerns reckoning for corrupt deeds; wealth cannot help, and only actions grounded in faith and sincerity can save.
rows.anchor: لا ينفعه مال ولا غيره , ولا ينجيه إلا ما كان من أعماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will extract, distinguish, and collect every good or evil intention hidden in the heart, revealing it in the record; this shows intentions are reckoned just like their outward effects.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن النيات يحاسب بها كما يحاسب على ما يظهر من آثارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's emphatic knowledge encompasses people inwardly and outwardly; the fronted phrase does not restrict His knowledge but stresses its full extent, so He judges to prevent good and evil from being treated alike.
rows.anchor: قدم هذا الجار والمجرور لا للاختصاص , بل للإشارة إلى نهاية الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment day makes everyone recognize God's complete knowledge of hidden and visible states, unlike worldly heedlessness when people forget that He sees them; the surah's close returns to its opening.
rows.anchor: فكيف بظواهرها جواهر وأعراضا , أقوالا وأفعالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated kalla intensifies the rebuke against rivalry; the particle can also mean truly or indeed, as some reciters explain.
rows.anchor: الأداة الصالحة له ولأن تكون لمعنى - حقا كما يقوله أئمة القراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If rivals gained certain knowledge even once, they would understand what awaits them, stop competing, weep more, and cry out in the open; the omitted answer and object emphasize that no certainty other than this matters and their conduct shows disbelief.
rows.anchor: لو يقع لكم علم على - وجه اليقين مرة من الدهر

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi calls certainty the vehicle of the path, the highest station of ordinary believers and the first step of the elect; the Prophet said it is the best thing placed in the heart.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : واليقين مركب الأخذ في هذا الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by mentioning distraction and omitting its cause, then mentioning knowledge as the fruit and omitting its consequence, freedom from distraction.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر الإلهاء أولا وحذف سببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The laam introduces a certain threat, not the conditional's answer: everyone will see Hell unveiled; believers escape it while disbelievers remain in it.
rows.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون هذا جوابا لما قبله لأنه محقق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Razi says direct vision replaces inference and report with observation, which breaks through the veil of knowledge; the second vision may alternatively mean touching or entering Hell.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : وهو المغني بالاستدراك عن الاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second seeing is eye-certainty: direct vision, the highest and doubt-free degree of knowledge; it may alternatively mean physical contact or entry, with the believer passing through and the disbeliever remaining.
rows.anchor: الرؤية التي هي نفس اليقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seeing Hell, people are questioned about every blessing, including cool water in summer and warm water in winter, and whether they used it extravagantly or to gain strength for good; obedient believers are honored, while sinners are reproached.
rows.anchor: الذي أداكم التكاثر إليه حتى عن الماء البارد في الصيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra's report says the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar visited Abu al-Haytham ibn al-Tayyihan, ate fresh and ripe dates, drank cool water, and sat in shade; the Prophet identified these as blessings subject to questioning.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي هرير رضي الله عنه عند الترمذي وغيره أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضاف أبا الهيم بن التيهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report through Mahmud ibn Labid with a chain the author calls good says people wondered what blessing remained beyond dates, water, and swords, and were told they would be questioned about it.
rows.anchor: كما في حديث محمود بن لبيد رضي الله عنه عند أحمد من وجه حسن إن شاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation cites corroborating versions at al-Tabarani from Ibn al-Zubayr and from al-Hasan al-Basri as a mursal report.
rows.anchor: له شاهد عند الطبراني عن ابن الزبير رضي الله عنهما , وعند الطبراني أيضا عن الحسن البصري مرسلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ending returns to the opening with a subtle warning: knowing every pleasure will be questioned restrains indulgence, even in permissible things, all the more so in disliked or forbidden things, especially when the questioner is the majestic King and questioning can lead to punishment.
rows.anchor: العاقل إذا علم أن بين يديه سؤالا عن كل ما يتلذذ به علم أنه يعوقه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fīl continues al-Humaza by showing God destroying those who trusted wealth and worldly allies; once such means fail, His power alone prevails.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر الهمزة من إهلاك المكاثرين في دار التعاضد والتناصر بالأسباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Elephant clearly signals this point when one considers the chapter, its army's story, and its appearance.
rows.anchor: واسمها الفيل ظاهر الدلالة على ذلك بتأمل سورته ، وما حصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala describes God's encompassing power, universal blessing, and complete mercy reserved for His elect.
rows.anchor: الذي له الإحاطة فقدرته في كل شيء عاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event makes visible al-Humaza's warning that wealth and human power can bring ruin; worldly prestige increases harm by encouraging rebellion against God, and Quraysh knew this event well.
rows.anchor: محذرا من الوجاهة في الدنيا وعلو الرتبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet did not witness the event, but knew it as if present through its آثار, widespread transmission, and God's informing him; its true lesson is known and acted upon by him and those God guides.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم وإن لم يشهد تلك الوقعة فإنه شاهد آثارها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with sukūn on the rāʾ of tar is reported to display the jussive effect and urge swift attention, since the army's destruction was as brief as a blink.
rows.anchor: وقرئ ( تر ) باسكان الراء , قالوا جدا في إظهار أثر الجازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative kayfa directs attention to the manner of God's act and its proofs of knowledge, power, prophetic foreshadowing, and honor for the Prophet and his city; the question clause suspends the governing verb.
rows.anchor: للناظر في الكيفية من التدقيق والوقوف على التحقيق في وجوه الدلالات على كمال علم الله وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God the Prophet's Lord points to His beneficence through this extraordinary event as a precursor to prophethood, and contrasts Him with idols called lords; disbelievers will know this with certainty when the Prophet is given the Sacred City.
rows.anchor: أي المحسن إليك ومن إحسانه إحسانه إلى قومك بك وبهذه الواقعة الخارقة للعادة إرهاصا لنبوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the Elephant were Abyssinians who had taken Yemen under their control; their emir, Abrahah al-Ashram, built a church in Sana'a called al-Qullays to divert pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: وهم الحبشة الذين كانوا غلبوا على بلاد اليمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The church's name al-Qullays is linked to qalas, a mouthful of fluid rising in the throat before vomiting; its name foreshadowed the ruin of its builder.
rows.anchor: تسميتها هذا الاسم الذي هو مشتق من القلس الذي أحد معانيه أنه ماء خرج من الحلق ملء الفم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrahah marched to destroy the Kaaba with many elephants, including the huge elephant Mahmūd; after subduing the Arabs, he was met at al-Mughammas by ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
rows.anchor: فخرج بجيشه لهدم بيت الله الكعبة ومعه أفيال كثيرة منه فيل عظيم اسمه محمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report says ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib offered a third of Tihama's wealth for Abrahah to withdraw; another says Abrahah's vanguard had taken two hundred camels, and their recovery became the immediate request.
rows.anchor: فعرض عليه ثلث أموال تهامة على أن يرجع عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrahah rebuked ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib for asking about his camels rather than the Kaaba; he replied that he owned the camels while the House had its own Lord, then recovered them and told Quraysh to flee to the mountains.
rows.anchor: فزهدت فيك حين تكلمني في مائتي بعير , وتترك كلامي

rows.speaker: عبد المطلب
rows.claim: At the Kaaba's ring, ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib prayed that God protect His sanctuary from the attackers and their cross and force.
rows.anchor: يا رب لا أرجو لهم سواكا فامنعهم أن يقربوا قراكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the army prepared to enter the sanctuary, the elephant knelt and would not move toward it, but ran when pointed elsewhere; it knelt again whenever turned toward the Haram.
rows.anchor: فوجهوه إلى غير الحرم فقام يهرول فوجهوه إلى الحرم فبرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent flocks of birds carrying one stone in each beak and two on their feet; stones between a lentil and chickpea in size pierced the attackers, killing them all while Meccans and Arabs watched from the mountains.
rows.anchor: كل طائر منها في منقاره حجر , وفي رجليه حجران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event occurred in the year of Muhammad's birth and was a foreshadowing of his prophethood.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك إرهاصا لنبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: حمزة الكرماني
rows.claim: Hamza al-Kirmani cites a narration placing the event on the very day of the Prophet's birth.
rows.anchor: وقال حمزة الكراماني : وفي رواية : يوم مولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The defeat enabled Sayf ibn Dhi Yazan to obtain a Persian force and eliminate the remaining Ethiopians; Quraysh, led by ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, later congratulated him, and he foretold the birth of Muhammad, his prophethood, and migration to Yathrib.
rows.anchor: وكأنه كان سببا لضعهم حتى ذهب سيف بن ذي يزن إلى كسرى وأتى منه بجيش فاستأصل بقيتهم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Al-Zubayr connects al-Humaza's deluded hoarders with the Elephant army, whose confidence in numbers and territorial power led them to attack the sanctuary and suffer swift destruction.
rows.anchor: لما تضمنت سورة الهمزة ذكر اغترار من فتن بماله حتى ظن أنه يخلده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their strategy was to disable the Kaaba by destroying it and redirecting pilgrimage to their church; their impressive worldly power ended in the failure and loss of that plan.
rows.anchor: أي في تعطيل الكعبة بتخريبها وبصرف الحج إلى كنيستهم على زعمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode warns that anyone attacking God's sanctities, including His house, a friend of God, or a religious scholar, is met by God's counterplot and harmed by his own malice.
rows.anchor: كل من تعرض لشيء من حرمات الله كبيت من بيوته أو ولي من أوليائه أو عالم من علماء الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He invokes the divine report, Whoever antagonizes one of My allies, I have declared war on him, as support for the warning against attacking God's friends.
rows.anchor: من عادى لي وليا فقد آذنته بالحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Openly committing sin hastens destruction more than concealing it; God can bring punishment from where it is not expected, so no one should feel secure even if the opponent seems weak.
rows.anchor: من جاهر بالمعصية أسرع إليه الهلاك بخلاف من تستر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prior clause implies God kept the army from entering Abraham's sanctuary or reaching the Messenger's city; the past-tense coordination means the same thing and is more explicit and apt.
rows.anchor: فمنعهم من الدخول إلى حرم إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام فضلا عن الوصول غلى بلده الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Birds were sent to humble people who had magnified themselves: God used creatures that ordinarily could not kill such an army.
rows.anchor: معلما بأنه سلط عليهم ما لا يقتل مثله في العادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayr is a collective noun masculine by form and feminine by sense, and may denote one bird; abābīl are vast, successive flocks from different directions, led by a distinctive bird.
rows.anchor: وهو اسم جمع يذكر على اللفظ , ويؤنث على المعنى

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says abābīl can describe horses coming from here and there; it is the plural of ibāla, a large bundle, as in the proverb about one hardship piled upon another.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : يقال : جاءت الخيل أبابيل من هاهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stones were numerous in impact but small in size, roughly a lentil, with one in each bird's beak and one in each foot.
rows.anchor: عظيمة في الكثرة والفعل , صغيرة في المقدار والحجم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sijjīl is hardened clay, fashioned for punishment in an elevated place, as further explained in Sūrat Hūd.
rows.anchor: طين متحجر مصنوع للعذاب في موضع هو في غاية العلو كما بين في سورة هود

rows.speaker: حمزة الكرماني
rows.claim: Hamza al-Kirmani transmits from Abu Salih that he saw the stones marked with red lines.
rows.anchor: قال حمزة الكرماني : قال أبو صالح : رأيت تلك الحجارة مخططة بالحمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The birds' attack caused their destruction through God's creative power, since the stones' ordinary effect would not cause such mass death.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك بفعل الله سبحانه وتعالى القادر على ما أراد لأنه الذي خلق الأثر قطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image may mean leaves hollowed by worms, a grain husk emptied of its kernel, or straw eaten and excreted by livestock; the hot stones pierced from head to rear and left black cavities.
rows.anchor: ورق زرع وقع فيه الأكال وهو أن يأكله الدود ويجوفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic description follows its decorum by comparing them to what has been eaten, as in the statement that Jesus and his mother ate food.
rows.anchor: ولكنه جاء على ما عليه آداب القرآن كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's ending and opening are joined by the wonder prompted by this extraordinary destruction, so its two ends embrace one another.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإهلاك في إعجابه هو من معاني الاستفهام التقريري في أولها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next surah presents the opposite side of al-Fīl: destruction of hostile deniers serves the flourishing of intimate worshippers, especially Quraysh, whose honor in both abodes is announced.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على ضد ما دلت عليه الفيل بأن إهلاك الجاحدين المعاندين لإصلاح المقربين العابدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Quraysh signals their status, and naming them rather than saying your people or al-Hums suggests they dominate all people both by strength and, as the Elephant story shows, without it.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بقريش دون قومك أو الحمس مثلا ونحوه دال على أنهم يغلبون الناس أجمع بقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's aim is to show the opposite of al-Fīl: hostile disbelievers are destroyed to restore the condition of devoted worshippers, and Quraysh receive glad tidings of honor in both abodes.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على ضد ما دلت عليه الفيل بأن إهلاك الجاحدين المعاندين لإصلاح المقربين العابدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title Quraysh points to their status; naming them rather than the Prophet's people or al-Hums implies they overcome all people both by strength and without it, as the Elephant event done for them shows.
rows.anchor: والتعبير بقريش دون قومك أو الحمس مثلا ونحوه دال على أنهم يغلبون الناس أجمع بقوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The basmala attributes all perfection and general blessings of creation and clarification to God, while describing His special favor as drawing whom He wills near and granting happiness.
rows.anchor: ذي النعم العامة بالإيجاد والبيان فهو ذو الأفضال
